text:
emma: Hey support — long generation requests keep failing with ReadTimeout after ~30s. Using redwood==0.5.1 on Python 3.11. I called client.generate(..., timeout=60) but still see the error. Any tips?

maria: Hi emma, sorry about that. Can you paste a minimal repro? Also which API method are you calling — streaming or non-streaming?

emma: Non-streaming initially, then tried streaming. Minimal snippet below (sanitized keys):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED", timeout=60)
resp = client.generate(model="gpt-large", prompt="Long story...", max_tokens=800)
print(resp.text)
```
Traceback: requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='api.redwood.ai', port=443): Read timed out.

jack: Two common gotchas: 1) the Python requests timeout semantics allow either a single float (total) or a tuple (connect, read). Some SDK versions treat the client.timeout as a total seconds int and others pass it through — so passing a tuple might be ignored depending on version. 2) We have a LB/socket idle read cutoff around 30s in some infra configs; long token generations can hit that if the server doesn't flush interim chunks.

ryan: Also note we changed a kwarg name in newer SDKs: redwood 0.6.x renamed the client arg from timeout -> request_timeout and adjusted retry wrapping. If you're on 0.5.x, passing the newer name won't do anything. Run `pip show redwood` to confirm.

maria: For your case, try either increasing the total timeout or, if your SDK supports it, passing a tuple for connect/read. Examples to try depending on SDK: 
- redwood 0.5.x: `RedwoodClient(..., timeout=600)` (total)
- redwood 0.6.x+: `RedwoodClient(..., request_timeout=(5,600))` (connect, read)
For streaming use `stream=True` and the SDK will keep the connection open; set a larger read timeout for that.

emma: I tried `timeout=(5,600)` and got `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'` which was odd.

jack: That error usually means the client code expected a number, not a tuple. Confirmed you said 0.5.1 — that version doesn't accept a tuple. Use the single-number total timeout or upgrade.

emma: OK I upgraded to redwood==0.6.2 and used `request_timeout=(5,600)` and the streaming generation no longer times out after 30s. Looks good. Thanks!

emma: One follow-up — I noticed enabling SDK retries caused a second request to be issued when the first timed out, so I think I got charged twice for the same user action. Is that expected?

maria: Good question. Two things: the SDK has retry policies and they are idempotency-aware — for non-idempotent endpoints (like generate) we disable aggressive retries by default, but network-layer retries can still occur if you enable them. For hosted billing we bill on tokens actually generated by the model; duplicate requests that cause additional generations can increase usage. Best practices: avoid automatic retries for long-running generate calls; if you must, use an idempotency key and the server-side operation status API when available.

ryan: I've created a short internal doc with examples and a compatibility table (0.5.x vs 0.6.x) and will link it in devex. Snapshot: https://redwood.internal/devex/py-timeout-guidance (internal). Tagging engineering to consider clearer error messages when an unsupported timeout shape is passed.

infra-bot: incident-check: no infra incidents in the last 24h.

maria: Summary / recommended steps for others who hit this: 
1) Check `pip show redwood` to get your SDK version.
2) If on 0.5.x: set a larger numeric `timeout` on the client (total seconds).
3) If on 0.6.x+: prefer `request_timeout=(connect_s, read_s)` for fine-grained control.
4) For streaming, use stream APIs and increase read timeout.
5) Avoid blind retries for long gens; prefer idempotency keys or operation-polling.

emma: Thanks everyone — resolved after upgrade and adjusting request_timeout. Appreciated!
